primitives.name: Team Cohesion Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: It marked an epoch in the career of athletics at Rutgers, an epoch where the prevailing characteristics were plenty of material, earnest co-operation between faculty, alumni, coaches and team, a marvelous coaching staf, absence of dissension and the hearty and active support of the student body.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'dimensionless cohesion strength parameter', 't': 'time variable in game epochs'}
primitives.assumptions: C(t) is a monotonically increasing function of institutional alignment and internal consistency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: C(t) → 0 when dissent or resource depletion occurs.

layer2.telemetry: Observable via institutional review scores and alumni participation metrics

primitives.name: Seasonal Performance Entropy
primitives.verbatim_quote: J.—The Targum, Rutgers College official organ, in its review of the 1914 season, says: 'The season was undoubtedly the most successful in the history of the college.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H': 'entropy of performance outcomes', 'p_i': 'probability of outcome i'}
primitives.assumptions: H = -Σ p_i log(p_i), with uniform distribution indicating maximum entropy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: H approaches zero when outcomes are deterministic or highly predictable.

layer2.mapping: H = -Σ p_i log(p_i) maps to variance in game results over season
layer2.telemetry: Variance in win/loss records and margin distributions

primitives.name: Tactical Execution Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: Washington and Jefferson displayed a lightning back-field and a wonderfully developed and varied forward pass, while the Scarlet demonstrated its great power in line-plunging and in steady team work.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E': 'efficiency of tactical execution', 'v': 'velocity vector of play', 'd': 'distance covered in play'}
primitives.assumptions: E ∝ v/d under constant resistance conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: E → 0 when play fails to generate forward progress.

layer2.telemetry: Average yards per play and turnover rates

C acts as a stabilizing kernel that reduces H by minimizing unpredictable variance in outcomes. E is a derived measure of strategic coherence, dependent on both individual skill and collective coordination. H quantifies the disorder or uncertainty in performance outcomes, inversely related to C. The interplay between these three constructs reveals a dynamic equilibrium where high cohesion supports high tactical execution, which leads to more predictable and stable seasonal performance. Failure modes include loss of cohesion leading to tactical inefficiencies and increased entropy, or excessive entropy masking underlying structural strengths.
